legend.text: Ten views of one system. Colour means the same thing on every page; position means ownership; an arrow is reserved for the relationships position cannot express.

legend.note: three conventions, and that is the whole vocabulary
solid carries traffic or creates; dashed only references
generated from the repos, not drawn by hand

legend.text: A dashed box is a boundary
Inside it means owned by it
legend.sub: no arrow needed to say so

legend.text: A filled box is the point
legend.sub: the two or three that matter
solid — A creates or calls B
not from a doc that drifted

legend.title: Why ten views and not one
legend.body: No single diagram of this system is both complete and readable. Each page answers one question and drops everything irrelevant to it, which is why the same component appears on several pages wearing different detail.

org.text: Every repo plays one of three roles: what the factory consumes, what it produces, or the factory itself. The deploy substrate sits between them.

org.note: the vocabulary the factory designs against
slow-moving cloud + cluster layers — shared by every tenant
standalone repos, each a Helm chart + a Platform CR

substrate.text: landing-zone, by layer. Organization components run once in the management account; everything below them is per-environment.

substrate.note: one VPC per environment — owned or adopted
a tenant's stores are a declaration, not a component

substrate.title: A tenant is a declaration
substrate.body: Adding a tenant edits a map. Its databases, buckets, queues and caches are written on Platform.spec.datastores and provisioned by the generic tenant-substrate module — there is no per-app component to write.

network.text: One component, two modes. In create mode it owns a VPC; in adopt mode it builds nothing and re-exports someone else's through the same outputs.

network.note: management account — the address space and the backbone
the single-account default — this component owns the VPC
network-owner account — the far side of adopt
one hub per transit gateway — every environment shares its NAT IPs

network.text: The cluster that lands on it
network.note: wires against one output contract either way

network.sub: fails at plan, not at apply

addons.text: One ApplicationSet per group, ordered by sync wave. A cluster opts in with a label; the generators do the rest.

addons.note: nothing else can reconcile until these are up
nodes, then the rules that govern them
the OTLP waist and its backends
workflow engine, then the dashboards that read it

addons.title: Two gateways, never both
addons.body: otel-gateway and otel-gateway-floor answer on the same telemetry.monitoring alias, and their ApplicationSets select mutually exclusive tiers. A tenant chart is byte-identical across them.

addons.title: The wave is the contract
addons.body: A cluster opts in with one label and the generators do the rest. Ordering lives in the sync-wave annotation, so ArgoCD enforces it rather than anyone remembering an install order.

control-plane.text: One binary, nine reconcilers, one leader-election lease. Each zone below is a reconciler; what sits inside it is what that reconciler creates and keeps true.

control-plane.note: three capability groups under nanohype.dev — the whole public API
the three loops that can stop a tenant
resolved at the top of every workload reconcile

control-plane.title: Why one binary
control-plane.body: Nine reconcilers share a single leader-election lease. Splitting them is trivial if one outgrows the rest; running six deployments before that happens is just more to operate.

control-plane.title: Fast state here, slow state in OpenTofu
control-plane.body: Per-tenant IAM, KMS grants and model access reconcile through the AWS SDK because a Platform apply must not wait on a Terragrunt run. Buckets, keys, endpoints and the event bus stay in landing-zone.

request-path.text: One invocation, app to model and back. The app holds no AWS credential and signs nothing — the gateway does, as the tenant.

request-path.note: inference leaves the cluster; nothing else does
the record the agent's account gets checked against

request-path.sub: run as the tenant, not a server

request-path.title: Steps 2 and 3 are where this breaks
request-path.body: extproc registers a body-parsing processor per endpoint path. A request to an unregistered prefix never has its model read out of the body, never gets x-ai-eg-model, and matches no route — so every call fails while the Gateway still reports healthy.

request-path.title: The app signs nothing
request-path.body: It holds no AWS credential. Envoy signs SigV4 as the tenant ServiceAccount, so the audit record and the agent's own account of what it did name the same principal.

identity.text: Isolation is a spectrum, not a boolean. Two orthogonal dials — where the control-plane CRs live, and how hard the workload boundary is.

identity.note: no role ARN is ever pasted into a chart
every Resource scoped by naming convention or exact ARN
a breach of the auditor role surfaces history, not content
growing up a tier is a value change, never a migration
the boundary the tenant cannot reach around
guardrails no workload role can escape

observability.text: One neutral waist. Producers emit OTLP to a stable alias; which backends exist behind it is a property of the cluster tier.

observability.note: telemetry.monitoring.svc:4317 — the same name in every tier
the tier is which of these exist
burn rate is not just an alert here

governance.text: Budget, SLO, and eval each close a loop that can stop a tenant. Recovery from the budget one is exclusively human.

governance.note: AWS-side only — it cannot reach the cluster
no CR mutation, no API path back

governance.title: Why the switch takes the long way
governance.body: EventBridge cannot call a Kubernetes API, so the switch only changes AWS state and the operator's existing loop picks the change up as drift. Nothing new is coupled to the cluster; the price is one reconcile interval of lag.

lifecycle.text: Two vending lines, one layer apart. Both write manifests to git; the cluster always wins on read.

lifecycle.note: a form, a CR, or a factory run
the source of truth for what should exist
ArgoCD applies; the operator reconciles what lands
